name: 10-sbml-nodes-uncoupled
title: SBML reactors on a network — uncoupled control (no diffusion)
question: With diffusion switched off, do the per-node oscillators stay out of phase?
hypothesis: Without inter-node transport each Repressilator runs independently, so nodes seeded at different phases never synchronise and the across-node spread stays large.
objective: Run the repressilator_network_uncoupled composite (SBML reactors + inter-node transport) and measure across-node synchrony.
description:
With diffusion off, the per-node oscillators remain independent and out of phase — the control that isolates coupling as the cause of synchronisation in study 09.

Each node runs the Repressilator SBML model integrated by COPASI (reusing viva-copasi); the NetworkTransport process diffuses proteins along edges. Reaction and diffusion are combined by operator splitting each tick. See viz/ for the concentration-on-network animation and the per-node time series.
claim: With diffusion off, the per-node oscillators remain independent and out of phase — the control that isolates coupling as the cause of synchronisation in study 09.

findings.name: repressilator_network_uncoupled-result
findings.summary: With diffusion off, the per-node oscillators remain independent and out of phase — the control that isolates coupling as the cause of synchronisation in study 09.
findings.detail: The same ring of Repressilators with diffusion disabled (D=0). Seeded at different phases, the nodes relax onto the common limit cycle (so the across-node spread dips from its initial transient value) but never phase-lock: a substantial spread persists (late across-node PX std ≈ 50), in sharp contrast to the coupled case where it collapses to ≈0. This control confirms the synchronisation in study 09 is caused by inter-node transport, not by the shared model.
